prompt.caption:
Genre preserve the supplied genre, period, and stylistic identity. Approximately 120 BPM. G major target key, in 4/4 timing. 1940s Soviet patriotic concert anthem, solemn minor-key verses rising into a triumphant major-key finale, and heroic disciplined choral performance. Favour enormous state concert hall acoustics, with the mix and spatial character appropriate to the stated era.
Vocals Base the lead and supporting vocal treatment on monumental all-male bass baritone and tenor choir. Treat lyric control tags such as Choir and Baritone as explicit performer or delivery changes; recurring named or gendered voices should remain recognisably stable. Keep lead, backing, choir, spoken, and character roles clearly separated, and use vocal effects only where they serve the stated style.
Arrangement Follow the lyric-section timeline Verse 1 → Verse 2 → Chorus → Verse 2 → Bridge → Verse 3 → Bridge → Verse 4 → Chorus → Outro. Transition: Vocal: Powerful all-male choir (bass, baritone, tenor); Transition: Instruments: Full orchestra, brass, snare drum, timpani, strings, accordion, low choir; Transition: Orchestral Introduction; Verse 1: Grand male choir; Bridge: Choir - Much Bigger; Outro: Massive orchestral ending. Instrument lifecycle full symphony orchestra, martial snare drum, timpani, commanding brass fanfares, sweeping strings, and accordion should enter, recede, and return as one evolving arrangement rather than remain as a static stack. Shape transitions through changes in density, register, articulation, percussion, and ambience so the energy curve remains clearly audible. Explicit exclusions avoid Hollywood trailer music, modern cinematic score, pop music, rock guitars, synthesizers, electronic percussion, female lead vocal, solo crooner, comedy novelty delivery, WESTERN, american.

lyrics.raw:
[verse]
[Choir]
From the throne upon the sofa,
She surveys the land once more.
Every hallway,
Every doorway,
Every rug from wall to wall.
[verse]
None may question,
None oppose her,
All rejoice beneath her reign.
Princess Beauts,
Great Gremlin Leader,
Guardian of treats and praise.
[chorus]
[Choir]
Glory! Glory!
Great Doja!
Leader of the Pack Union!
Strongest heart and clever mind,
Guide us through these peaceful times!
[chorus]
Glory! Glory!
Great Doja!
Every tail now wags as one!
Long may Princess Beauts command,
Brightest dog in all the land!
[verse]
When brave Chunk returns with treasure,
Bearing forth the sacred ball,
She accepts his humble offering,
For the good and joy of all.
Then with wisdom
Beyond measure,
She declares the royal fee:
"One Dentastix...
Many scratches...
Then perhaps this ball goes free."
[Choir]
Wise is Doja!
Strong is Doja!
Nothing happens by mistake!
Every scheme already planned,
Before the humans even wake!
[bridge]
Wise is Doja!
Strong is Doja!
Opossum Face forever reigns!
Every victory was foretold,
Inside her magnificent brain!
[verse]
Once there stood a mighty ladder,
Built for humans, tall and steep.
Others searched
For little dog doors...
Doja climbed the ladder.
The people watched in silent wonder.
The birds forgot their songs.
Even Chunk looked up in awe.
The Princess simply carried on.
[bridge]
[Choir]
Raise the banner!
Sound the brass!
Let the mighty chorus sing!
[verse]
She who conquered
Walls at Lyme,
She who made the Gremlin spring!
River waters cannot tame her!
Rain awakens glorious might!
Digging, charging,
Leading chaos,
Victory in every fight!
[Baritone]
Should the Chunk commit misfortune,
She need never bark or shout.
Just one gentle nudge upon your arm...
Justice finds him.
[chorus]
Glory! Glory!
Great Doja!
Supreme Leader of the Pack!
Every cushion,
Every blanket,
Every sunny patch is hers!
Treats are hers!
Scratches hers!
Walks begin upon command!
[outro]
Long live Princess Beauts forever!
Long live Gremlin Leader!
Long live Doja!
DOJA!
DOJA!
DOJA!
(Choir holds final chord)
